### Introduction

This week, your assignment is to begin manipulating data in R. You will also learn how to import data from .CSV files. Each week during these section times, you will work in pairs or small groups to complete the tasks.

Questions:

1. (1 point) Assign to a vector called X the values 1,3,5,6,7, and 9. Assign to a vector called Y the values 2,7,4,5,2 and 12. X has been done for you as an example.

```{r}
X<- c(1,3,5,6,7,9)
X
Y<- c(2,7,4,5,2,12)
Y
```

```{r}
### This chunk of code is for grading purposes. 
### Don't change/delete this chunk of code. 
q1 <- X
q2 <- Y
```

  

2. (1 point) Concatenate (combine) the two vectors(X and Y) together as one larger (length of 12) vector called Z.
```{r}
Z <- c(X,Y)
  
Z  
```


```{r}
### This chunk of code is for grading purposes. 
### Don't change/delete this chunk of code.

```

  
 
3. (1 point) Using R functions, calculate the mean of Z.
```{r}

meanZ
```

```{r}
### This chunk of code is for grading purposes.
```

4. (1 point) Create a new vector that includes all the values in Z that are less than 7.

```{r}
newZ
```


12. Give an example of a scientific inductive model (We discussed the periodic table in class, so that one is off-limits for this question!). Explain how this model has changed since its first publication. Cite the source you used to answer this question!

```{r}
q12 <- "The Human Genome Project is an example of a scientific inductive model, because it was created from a series of experiments and observations testing the genomes of subjects, and was constantly updated with new information. It has changed over time to more accurately and fully represent the genetic sequences and DNA of humans. Citation: https://www.genome.gov/human-genome-project"
```
